matches.original: Justice in Baldwin County depends on who you know, not what the law actually says. Paul Ripp’s letter to DA Robert Wilters exposes how Marcus McDowell and Judge Stankoski manipulated the legal clock to let Ronan McSharry’s criminal appeal die in the shadows without a single day of jail.
matches.brief:
THE CONFLICT:
- Ronald McSharry (Ronan McSharry) convicted in Fairhope Municipal Court March 26 for assault of Paula DiNardi (November 23, 2018 at Little Whiskey Christmas Club).
- Fairhope City Council appointed Municipal Judge and City Attorney (Marcus McDowell), who failed to defend victim according to Ripp Report.
- Judge J. Clark Stankoski issued Order dismissing McSharry’s appeal denovo due to 365-day statute of limitations expiration.
- Ripp Report alleges systemic corruption linked to "CATALYST" political influence in Fairhope City Council.
- Specific Council members targeted: Councilman Boone, Mayor (unnamed in text but referred to), Councilman Burrell.
- Ripp Report alleges McSharry is protected by "good ole boy politics."

THE DISCOVERY:
- Francis "Paul" Ripp sent formal letter dated April 24, 2020 to Baldwin County District Attorney Robert Wilters.
- Letter alleges McSharry is a repeat offender, green card holder, and on probation regarding prior harassment against Nall Hollis.
- Letter explicitly names City Attorney Marcus McDowell and Municipal Judge Snedeker as part of suspicious judicial operations.
- Letter claims McSharry hired attorneys to circumvent Alabama Source Shield Law against Ripp’s attorney Harry Still.
- Evidence confirms public opinion in Fairhope views McSharry assault on DiNardi as jealousy-driven retaliation regarding Tiki Bar business competition.

THE PIVOT:
- Article 2 (Widget) formalizes the allegations made in Article 1 (Main) into a documented legal demand to DA Robert Wilters.
- Specific dates in Article 2 (Incident: Nov 23, 2018; Appeal Dismissal: after March 26 plea) confirm the timeline of corruption Article 1 is attacking.
- Ripp Report serves as primary investigator linking Judge Stankoski's order, McDowell’s actions, and CATALYST council appointments.
- Letter confirms Ripp Report is financially/legally invested (consumer advocate for DiNardi, Nall Hollis), validating their investigative stance on the Fairhope justice system.

THE PIVOT:

matches.brief:
THE CONFLICT:
- Nov 22/23, 2018: Ronan McSherry shoved Paula Dinardi off a bar stool at Little Whiskey Christmas Club in Fairhope; incident captured on video surveillance.
- McSherry had prior arrest record for harassment against Nall Hollis; probation violated penalty was 180 days jail.
- March 26, 2019: Fairhope Municipal Court; McSherry pleaded guilty to assault.
- Municipal Judge Snedeker sentenced McSherry to 180 days, credited two months for alleged rehab time.
- City Attorney Marcus McDowell failed to amend Fairhope charging document for over a year (365 days) to include “did cause bodily harm.”

THE DISCOVERY:
- April 24, 2020: the Ripp Report submitted a formal demand letter to Baldwin County District Attorney Robert Wilters.
- The Letter confirms Baldwin County Circuit Judge J. Clark Stankoski dismissed McSherry’s appeal denovo based on technicality that the City was outside its 365-day window to amend charging document.
- The Letter asserts no double jeopardy applies because Stankoski’s order was “pre-trial” (before jury struck).
- The Letter requests Wilters to take the case back to a grand jury and recharge McSherry.
- The Letter flags that civil motion is underway; Stankoski ordered attorney Harry Still to turn over communications with Lagniappe, testing Alabama Source Shield Law.

THE PIVOT:
- The April 24 Letter transforms the Main Article's suspicion into a formal legal escalation.
- It identifies specific gaps in the Main Article’s narrative by naming dates (Nov 23, 2018 vs March 26) and confirming McDowell’s specific failure regarding the charge.
- It serves as the "smoking gun" because it forces an official record of Ripp’s claim: that Stankoski used a procedural loophole to let McSherry off, rather than correcting the charging document McDowell botched.
- It links the judicial trickery directly to a demand for the District Attorney’s office to intervene where they currently see no accountability.

matches.original: The May primary offers a rare chance to break the Sheriff Department's twenty-year streak of zero accountability. State records show Francis Ripp formally warned Secretary Wes Allen that Anthony Lowery holds total control over the very ballot boxes used in rigged elections.
matches.brief:
THE CONFLICT:
- Baldwin County Sheriff Huey "Hoss" Mack served as top law enforcement officer for approximately 17 years (retired July 2024) to become executive director of the Alabama Sheriffs Association.
- Mack's departure was mid-term; he resigned to seek another political position (executive director role).
- Governor Kay Ivey appointed Anthony Lowery to fill the vacancy effective September 1, 2024. Lowery had ~20 years at BCSO (Civil Affairs Commander 2007, Chief Deputy 2018).
- Ripp Report claims BCSO built a "culture of absolute immunity" with no transparency or accountability; BCSO investigates itself via the Major Crimes Division.
- Culture attributed to Mack and passed to Lowery: self-investigation, suppressed exculpatory evidence, wrongful convictions (example: Murray Lawrence Jr., 20+ years in prison for a murder he did not commit; Lowery was lead investigator).
- Political "good ole boy" cabal described as Stacy/Elliott/Haygood, then "Catalyst," now Scott Boone Consulting, controlling county office elections.

THE DISCOVERY:
- May 17, 2026 letter to Alabama Secretary of State Wes Allen and Director of Elections Jeff Elrod by the Ripp Report (33 years of experience).
- Letter states the primary election cycle had "more public participation than in any election in 20 years plus," with most attention on the Sheriff's race.
- The Ripp Report claims it has been "in contact with the Sec of State in reference to suspected and strongly alleged reports of elections being fixed involving numerous races in Baldwin County, in the past."
- Letter notes the sheriff is the custodian of ballot boxes, which "raises red flags right away" given 20-year BCSO culture of no transparency/accountability.
- Elrod  explained safeguards in place and advised Ripp to follow up with Baldwin County officials (Ripp claims this was done).
- Ripp asks Allen/Elrod to take complaints of voter fraud in any Baldwin County primary election seriously, citing "33 years of experience" as reason for caution.

THE PIVOT:
- Article 1 frames the May 19 primary as a chance to break the "Good Ole Boy culture" and end a "20 year culture of BCSO" with no transparency or accountability. It urges voters to support Matt McKenzie (vs. Lowery) for Sheriff and other anti-incumbent candidates, and warns voters to watch for "alleged rigged elections, fixed qualifications and absentee boxes regulated by the GOB."
- Article 2 is the smoking gun because it formally documents Ripp's direct contact with the state election officials about suspected past election-fixing in Baldwin County, tying the same BCSO custody-of-ballots problem to actual voter fraud allegations. It converts the "conspiracy" language of Article 1 into a documented request for investigation by the Secretary of State, giving concrete credibility and an official channel (Wes Allen / Jeff Elrod) for the complaints that Article 1 only alludes to.

KEY ENTITIES:
